t.1.59.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Indra made an agreement with Nārāyaṇa that, together with the gods, they would descend from heaven to the earth through portions of themselves.
t.1.59.2: And Śakra himself, having instructed all the dwellers of heaven, went forth again from that abode of Nārāyaṇa.
t.1.59.3: For the destruction of the enemies of the immortals and for the welfare of all the worlds, those dwellers of heaven descended in due order from heaven to this earth.
t.1.59.4: Then, O tiger among kings, the dwellers of heaven took birth as they wished in the lineages of brahmin seers and in the families of royal seers.
t.1.59.5: They slew Dānavas and Rākṣasas, Gandharvas and Pannagas as well, and other man-eating creatures in great numbers.
t.1.59.6: The Dānavas and Rākṣasas, and likewise the Gandharvas and serpents, could not slay them, who were mighty even in childhood, O best of the Bharatas.
t.1.59.7: Of the hosts of Devas and Dānavas, and likewise of the Gandharvas and Apsarases, of all men as well, and likewise indeed of the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas...
t.1.59.8: I wish to hear truly, from the beginning, the complete origin of all living beings in every respect, for you are all-knowing.
t.1.59.9: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Well then, having bowed to Svayaṃbhū, the Self-Existent, I shall tell you properly of the origin and dissolution of the gods and the other beings of the worlds.
t.1.59.10: The six great seers are known as the mind-born sons of Brahmā: Marīci, Atri and Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, and Kratu.
t.1.59.12: Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kālā, Anāyus, Siṃhikā, Muni, Krodhā, Prāvā, and Ariṣṭā, and likewise Vinatā and Kapilā.
t.1.59.13: And Kadrū too, O tiger among men, was a daughter of Dakṣa, O Bhārata. The sons and grandsons of these women, endowed with valor, are without end.
t.1.59.11: Kaśyapa was the son of Marīci, and from Kaśyapa these creatures were born; the illustrious daughters of Dakṣa, thirteen in number, were their mothers.
t.1.59.14: From Aditi were born the twelve Ādityas, lords of the worlds; those, O king, I shall proclaim to you by name, O Bhārata.
t.1.59.15: Dhātṛ, Mitra, Aryaman, Śakra, Varuṇa, and Aṃśa too, Bhaga, Vivasvant, and Pūṣan, and likewise Savitṛ as the tenth.
t.1.59.16: Likewise Tvaṣṭṛ is the eleventh, and Viṣṇu is said to be the twelfth; though the last-born of all the Ādityas, he surpasses them all in virtues.
t.1.59.17: Hiraṇyakaśipu is remembered as the one and only son of Diti, and these five sons of that great-souled one are renowned by name.
t.1.59.18: Prahrāda was the eldest of them, and Saṃhrāda came immediately after him; Anuhrāda was the third, and after him came Śibi and Bāṣkala.
t.1.59.19: Prahrāda had three sons, renowned everywhere, O Bhārata: they were celebrated as Virocana, Kumbha, and Nikumbha.
t.1.59.20: Virocana had a single son, the mighty Bali; and Bali's renowned son was the great asura named Bāṇa.
t.1.59.22: Śambara and Namuci, and the one renowned as Pulomā, Asilomā and Keśī, and the Dānava Durjaya as well.
t.1.59.21: Forty were the sons of Danu, renowned everywhere, O Bhārata; the firstborn of them was the king Vipracitti of great fame.
t.1.59.24: Svarbhānu, Aśva, Aśvapati, Vṛṣaparvan, and likewise Ajaka, Aśvagrīva, Sūkṣma, and the great Asura Tuhuṇḍa.
t.1.59.23: Ayaḥśiras, Aśvaśiras, and the valiant Ayaḥśaṅku; likewise Gaganamūrdhan, Vegavat, and he who was Ketumat.
t.1.59.26: Śarabha and Śalabha, and likewise Sūrya and Candramas: these are proclaimed as the renowned Dānavas in the lineage of Danu. But the Sūrya and Candramas of the gods are held to be another pair.
t.1.59.27: And these too, O great king, renowned in that lineage, were the ten sons of Danu, mighty and full of courage, bulls among the Dānavas.
t.1.59.25: Isṛpas and Ekacakra, Virūpākṣa, Hara and Ahara, Nicandra and Nikumbha, Kupatha, and likewise Kāpatha.
t.1.59.28: Ekākṣa, the hero Mṛtapā, Pralamba and Naraka too, Vātāpi, the scorcher of foes, and Śaṭha, the great Asura.
t.1.59.29: Gaviṣṭha, Danāyus, and the Dānava Dīrghajihva; their sons and grandsons are held to be countless, O Bhārata.
t.1.59.30: Siṃhikā bore a son, Rāhu, the crusher of the moon and the sun, and also Sucandra, Candrahantṛ, and Candravimardana.
t.1.59.33: The renowned sons of Kālā, like Death itself, were strikers in battle, famed on earth, of great valor, scorchers of foes among the Dānavas.
t.1.59.32: Anāyus, in turn, had four sons, bulls among the Asuras: Vikṣara, Bala and Vīra, and Vṛtra, the great Asura.
t.1.59.31: The cruel-natured, countless sons and grandsons of Krūrā formed the host named Krodhavaśa, cruel in deeds and crushers of their enemies.
t.1.59.34: Vināśana and Krodha, another who was the slayer of Krodha, and likewise yet another, Krodhaśatru: these are renowned as the Kāleyas.
t.1.59.35: Śukra, the son of a seer, became the preceptor of the Asuras; and the four sons of Uśanas were renowned as the sacrificial priests of the Asuras.
t.1.59.37: Thus has the origin of the lineages of the mighty Asuras and Suras been told to you, as I heard it in the Purāṇa.
t.1.59.36: Tvaṣṭṛ the younger, and likewise Atri, two others devoted to the rites of mantras, all of them like the sun in splendor and promoters of the world of Brahman.
t.1.59.38: But the offspring of these, O protector of the earth, cannot be counted in full, for it is endless and rich in virtues.
t.1.59.39: Tārkṣya and Ariṣṭanemi, and likewise Garuḍa and Aruṇa, Āruṇi and also Vāruṇi: these are remembered as the sons of Vinatā.
t.1.59.41: Bhīmasena and Ugrasena, Suparṇa and likewise Varuṇa, Gopati and Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Sūryavarcas as the seventh.
t.1.59.40: Śeṣa, Ananta, Vāsuki, the serpent Takṣaka, Kūrma and Kulika are the mighty sons of Kadrū.
t.1.59.42: Pattravān, Arkaparṇa, and the renowned Prayuta, and Bhīma and Citraratha, famed, all-knowing and self-controlled.
t.1.59.43: Likewise, O king, Śāliśiras, and Pradyumna as the fourteenth, Kali as the fifteenth, and Nārada as the sixteenth: these are celebrated as the divine Gandharvas, the sons of Muni.
t.1.59.44: Now, Bhārata, I shall tell you of other beings: Prāvā gave birth to Anavadyā, Anuvaśā, Anūnā, Aruṇā, Priyā, Anūpā, Subhagā, and Bhāsī.
t.1.59.46: Viśvāvasu and Bhānu, and likewise Sucandra as the tenth: these are proclaimed to be the divine Gandharvas born of Prādhā.
t.1.59.45: Siddha, Pūrṇa, Barhin, the greatly renowned Pūrṇāśa, Brahmacārin, Ratiguṇa, and Suparṇa as the seventh.
t.1.59.47: But this renowned race of the Apsarases, bearing auspicious marks, the illustrious goddess Prāvā bore long ago from the divine seer.
t.1.59.48: Alambusā, Miśrakeśī, Vidyutparṇā, Tulānaghā, Aruṇā, and Rakṣitā as well, Rambhā, and likewise Manoramā.
t.1.59.50: Amṛta, the brāhmaṇas, the cows, and likewise the Gandharvas and Apsarases are proclaimed in the Purāṇa to be the offspring of Kapilā.
t.1.59.49: Asitā and Subāhu, Suvratā and Subhujā, Supriyā and Atibāhu; and the famed pair Hahā and Huhū, and Tumburu: these four are remembered as the finest of the Gandharvas.
t.1.59.51: Thus I have told you the origin of all beings, and likewise the origin of the Gandharvas and Apsarases has been duly enumerated.
t.1.59.54: But whoever, observing the proper discipline, recites this lineage of the great-souled ones in the presence of brahmins and gods obtains abundant offspring, prosperity, and fame, and after death a splendid destiny.
t.1.59.52: Of the serpents, the Suparṇas, the Rudras and likewise the Maruts, of the cows and of the brāhmaṇas, glorious and of holy deeds.
t.1.59.53: It bestows long life, it is meritorious and auspicious, and it brings delight to the ear; it should always be listened to, and always be recited to others, by one who is free from envy.
